correctness.rationale: For a compactly supported invariant probability measure, stationarity of x, y, x^2/2, and xy gives the required mean identities. Averaging the z equation yields the stated defect law after exact factorization of the equilibrium quadratic. The observable z erf(z) is globally nonnegative and vanishes only at z=0, which supplies the threshold obstruction, endpoint rigidity, and variance bounds. At the discriminant boundary every nonnegative defect term vanishes; stationarity of xy then forces y=0, leaving only the double-equilibrium Dirac mass. The compact-set implication uses existence of an invariant probability measure on a nonempty compact invariant set. Exact-rational arithmetic for the hidden-parameter specialization was replayed successfully.

value.rationale: The source’s main application is the transition between self-excited and hidden chaotic regimes under the parameters mu and a1. The new theorem identifies the equilibrium discriminant as the exact existence threshold for all compact invariant dynamics, not merely for equilibria, and makes the threshold stationary state rigid. Above threshold it yields a sharp global mean/variance envelope for every compact recurrent statistical state, including the reported hidden regime. This directly constrains a central dynamical object of the source and is not a routine local-stability recomputation or arbitrary parameter slice.
